questions.q: In "Respect and dignity first Understand", which of these is a key idea?
o: Use a weekly pill box and a written list from the doctor or pharmacist.
Respond calmly to repeated questions; do not argue.
Call at once for chest pain, trouble breathing, stroke signs, serious bleeding or a head injury.
Ask how the person likes to be addressed and what matters to them.

questions.q: In "Home safety check Analyse", which of these is a key idea?
o: Offer enough time; rushing causes accidents and loss of confidence.
Access: keys for helpers, clear path for emergency crews, phone within reach.
Use calendars, clear labels and a daily board for memory.
Seek advice if mood or memory changes quickly.

questions.q: In "Daily living support Apply", which of these is a key idea?
o: Use aids: long-handled tools, easy-grip cutlery, pill boxes.
Join a carer group or call a helpline.
Update the plan and tell everyone involved.
Protect privacy in washing, dressing and toilet care.

questions.q: In "Medicines and health reminders Apply", which of these is a key idea?
o: Break tasks into steps and help with the step that is hard.
Note side effects such as dizziness, confusion or rash and report them.
Keep numbers, medical history and medicine list on a card by the phone.
Call at once for chest pain, trouble breathing, stroke signs, serious bleeding or a head injury.

questions.q: In "Mind, mood and memory Apply", which of these is a key idea?
o: Call the clinic the same day for fever, new confusion or a bad fall without injury.
Keep routine, light, daily walks and social contact.
Share tasks and agree a rota.
Access: keys for helpers, clear path for emergency crews, phone within reach.

questions.q: In "Emergencies and when to call Evaluate", which of these is a key idea?
o: Note side effects such as dizziness, confusion or rash and report them.
Fire and gas: working smoke alarm, safe cooking habits, switch-off reminders.
Seek advice if mood or memory changes quickly.
Call at once for chest pain, trouble breathing, stroke signs, serious bleeding or a head injury.

questions.q: In "Family and carer wellbeing Evaluate", which of these is a key idea?
o: Practise the plan with the family.
Offer enough time; rushing causes accidents and loss of confidence.
Take breaks, sleep and eat properly; ask for respite.
Note side effects such as dizziness, confusion or rash and report them.

questions.q: In "Review and improve Create", which of these is a key idea?
o: Update the plan and tell everyone involved.
Watch for stress signs such as anger, tiredness and withdrawal.
Watch eating, drinking, skin and sleep and record changes.
Use calendars, clear labels and a daily board for memory.
